title: Intermittent Fasting Calculator: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Intermittent Fasting Calculator](/intermittent-fasting-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Fasting and eating windows for 16:8, 18:6, 20:4 and 5:2 schedules. Enter your fasting plan and when does your eating window start? (24-hour, e.g. 12:00) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Plan an intermittent fasting schedule: pick a plan and the time your eating window starts, and see exactly when to eat and when to fast. In 16:8 you eat during an 8-hour window and fast for the other 16 — for example, eating from noon to 8 PM and fasting overnight. The calculator shows both windows for 14:10, 16:8, 18:6 and 20:4. Fasting does not suit everyone, and it is not a licence to eat anything: what you eat in the window still matters. This is an estimate for healthy adults, not medical advice. It does not suit children, pregnancy, eating disorders or anyone with a medical condition — talk to a doctor or registered dietitian before changing your diet or sleep habits.

## How to use the Intermittent Fasting Calculator

Start by choosing your fasting plan from the list, then typing or pasting your when does your eating window start? (24-hour, e.g. 12:00). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Choose a fasting plan — 16:8 is the usual starting point.
2. Enter the time your eating window starts.
3. Read your eating and fasting windows for the day.

## Formula

Eating window = start time to start time + eating hours. Fasting window = end of the eating window to the next day's start time. For 16:8 starting at noon: eat 12:00 PM – 8:00 PM, fast 8:00 PM – 12:00 PM.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Intermittent Fasting Calculator](/intermittent-fasting-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. On 16:8 with an eating window starting at 12:00 PM, you eat from 12:00 PM to 8:00 PM and fast from 8:00 PM until noon the next day. Try the same figures in the [Intermittent Fasting Calculator](/intermittent-fasting-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Fasting plan: 16:8 — fast 16 hours, eat in 8, When does your eating window start? (24-hour, e.g. 12:00): 12:00), the [Intermittent Fasting Calculator](/intermittent-fasting-calculator) returns Eating window: 12:00 PM – 8:00 PM, Fasting window: 8:00 PM – 12:00 PM, Fasting hours: 16 hours a day, Eating hours: 8 hours a day, Next fast starts: 8:00 PM. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Which plan to start with

Start with 14:10 or 16:8 — the gentler plans are much easier to stick to, and most of the benefit comes from simply not snacking late at night. Jumping straight to 20:4 usually ends in a binge and a abandoned plan. Give any plan two weeks before judging it: hunger is strongest in the first few days and fades as your body adapts to the schedule.

## What breaks a fast

Water, black coffee and plain tea do not break a fast. Anything with calories does — including milk in coffee, juice and “zero-calorie” drinks that are not truly zero. During the eating window, eat normally: fasting is about when you eat, not a reason to eat twice as much. If you feel dizzy, faint or unwell, eat and stop fasting.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Start with 14:10 or 16:8 — the gentler plans stick.
- Water, black coffee and plain tea are fine while fasting.
- Keep the same window every day so your body adapts.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is 16:8 intermittent fasting?

Eating during an 8-hour window each day and fasting for the other 16 hours — for example, eating from noon to 8 PM and fasting overnight. Try it with your own numbers in the [Intermittent Fasting Calculator](/intermittent-fasting-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What can I drink while fasting?

Water, black coffee and plain tea. Anything with calories — milk, juice, sugary drinks — breaks the fast. Try it with your own numbers in the [Intermittent Fasting Calculator](/intermittent-fasting-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is intermittent fasting safe?

For most healthy adults, yes. It does not suit children, pregnancy, eating disorders, diabetes on medication, or anyone who feels unwell while fasting — talk to a doctor first. Try it with your own numbers in the [Intermittent Fasting Calculator](/intermittent-fasting-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Do I need to count calories while fasting?

Fasting controls when you eat, not how much. If you eat more in the window than you used to eat all day, you will still gain weight. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
